spans.s: 1. mah-a, m. festival.

2. mah-á, a. great, abundant (RV.);
 n. pl. 🞄mighty deeds (RV.).

mah-ā, a. great (occurs as an independent 🞄adjective only in the RV. ac. mahā́m). 🞄This word is very frequent (being both V. and 🞄C.) ˚— in the sense of an adjective (great) or 🞄an adverb (greatly, very), mahat with few 🞄exceptions being used thus only in the sense 🞄of a substantive.
mahat-śabda, m. the title ‘Great.’
maha-tā, f. greatness.

mah-ana, n. praising;
 -anīya, fp. 🞄praiseworthy.
mah-ar, indecl. the fourth of the seven 🞄worlds in the ascending series.
mahar-loka, m. = mahar.

mahā‿ṛṣi, m. great sage;
 ep. of Śiva.

mahalla-ka, a. (ikā) feeble, weak, 🞄decrepit;
 ikā, f. N. of a daughter of Prahlāda.
mahas-vin, a. radiant, brilliant, 🞄lustrous.
mahikā, f. cold (only ˚—): -aṃśu, 🞄m. (cold-rayed), moon.
mah-i-ta, pp. (√ mah) honoured, etc..
mah-ilā, f. woman: -āropya, m. N. 🞄of a town in the South near Madras.

māhiṣa, a. (ī) belonging to or derived 🞄from the buffalo: i-ka, m. keeper of 🞄buffaloes;
 paramour of an unchaste woman.
mah-iṣṭha, spv. (of mahat) greatest.
mahī-kṛ, magnify.

mah-īyā́, f. joyfulness (V.);
 d. -īyaí.

mah-īyas, cpv. greater, larger, 🞄mightier, more powerful or important, etc.;
 🞄very great, — mighty, — distinguished, — loud 🞄(laughter), etc.
mah-é, d. inf. to rejoice (RV.).
mahā‿iccha, a. having high aims, 🞄ambitious: -tā, f. ambition.
mahelā, f. woman.

mahā‿aitareya, n. T. of a Vedic text;
 🞄-aiśvarya, n. great power.
mah-mán, m. greatness (AV.¹).
mah-ya, fp. highly honoured.
máhyam, d. of ahám, I.
mahlaṇa, m. N. of a king: -svāmin, 🞄m. N. of a temple built by him.
mahlāṇa-pura, n. N. of a town.
māhā-nāman-a, a. belonging 🞄to the Mahānāmnī verses.
māhitra, n. designation of RV. X, 185 (so called because it begins with the words 🞄‘mahi trīṇām’).

mā́hin-a, a. (RV.) glad, blithe, joyous;
 🞄gladdening (fr. mah-ín).
māhiṣ-mat-ī, f. N. of a city.
māhiṣ-ya, m. a. mixed caste (offspring 🞄of Kṣatriya and Vaiśyā).

māheya, a. [fr. mahī] earthen;
 m. 🞄met. son of earth, planet Mars.
